meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
The carp live in the bathtub.
They live wonderfully in the bathtub.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?
The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините.
+ accusative (кого).

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, excuse me, there's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: possessive adjective

examples.text: Вот этот тёплый мамин платок надо срочно починить!
examples.trans: This warm shawl of Mom's needs to be fixed urgently!

examples.text: Вика, ты как мамин платок на работе забыла?
examples.trans: Vika, how did you forget Mom's shawl at work?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
+ infinitive.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Parenthetical adverb.

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: in an awkward or embarrassed manner

examples.text: Да, под такую музыку обниматься немного неловко.
examples.trans: Yes, it is a bit awkward hugging to such music.
It turned out somewhat awkward, Kostya.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Our hotel has to impress the guests.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: Our hotel has a new service.

examples.text: Кто бы мог подумать, что буду управлять отелем?
examples.trans: Who'd have thought I'd be running a hotel?

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: declines like a feminine noun in -а, but is masculine

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!.

examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
I'll invite a female friend over.

examples.text: Пять тысяч рублей. Я подругу приглашу.
examples.trans: Five thousand roubles. I'll invite a female friend over.

meanings.note: + с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться').

examples.text: А как вы с ней познакомились?
examples.trans: And how did you meet her?
She was the one who met me!

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to have a drink, to drink a little
meanings.note: + accusative or partitive genitive: попить воды = have a drink of water

examples.trans: Is that how you went for a drink of water?

examples.text: Самсон, ты с ума сошёл? Ты так воды пошёл попить?
examples.trans: Samson, have you lost your mind? Is that how you went for a drink of water?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Asks about the reason.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'крыть').

examples.trans: He just wants to cover for me.

examples.text: Он просто хочет по-дружески прикрыть меня перед шефом.
examples.trans: He just wants to cover for me as a friend in front of the chef.

examples.text: Прикрой, пожалуйста, кастрюлю крышкой, чтобы бульон не остыл.
examples.trans: Please cover the pot with a lid so the broth does not get cold.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

проводить.gloss: to see off, to see out

meanings.en: to see someone out, to see off
meanings.note: accompany someone to the door or the station
a different, imperfective verb проводить means 'to conduct, to spend (time)'

examples.text: Держи свои духи. Давай я тебя провожу. Пока!
examples.trans: Here is your perfume. Let me walk you out. Bye!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Рано умер = died young / too early.

examples.text: Муж тоже там работал. И рано умер.
examples.trans: My husband worked there too. And he died young.
Tomorrow I need to get up early.

examples.text: Что, по домам? Мне завтра рано вставать.
examples.trans: What, time to go home? I have to get up early tomorrow.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу.

examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: Food, air, news.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative.
TV, a film.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: affectionate form of сын, often used as a form of address

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Если проблема только в этом, то да.
examples.trans: If that's the only problem, then yes.

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: Otherwise we were already starting to worry.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
